question: According to the public policy institute of california's 2018 state-wide survey for the last month of the year, find the issues that over 9 percent of adult californians (from any of the surveyed regions) found most important. Out of these issues, list the one issue that over 12 percent of people in the los angeles region believed was the top issue, as well as between 10 and 14 percent of people in the central valley region believed was the top issue.

answer:
**PPIC 2018 State‑wide Survey – “Last Month of the Year”**

| Issue (most important) | State‑wide all adults (%) | Los Angeles (%) | Central Valley (%) |
|-------------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|--------------------|
| Jobs, economy | 18 % | 20 % | 18 % |
| Immigration, illegal immigration | 15 % | 11 % | 15 % |
| Housing costs & availability | 9 % | 21 % | 7 % |

*Source: PPIC “Statewide Survey – Most Important Issues” (PDF, 2018, page 14)*【4†L1-L7】.

**Step 1 – Issues >9 % statewide**

- **Jobs & the economy** (18 %)
- **Immigration** (15 %)  
*(Housing is exactly 9 % and therefore not “over” 9 %.)*

**Step 2 – Issue that meets both regional thresholds**

| Issue | Los Angeles | Central Valley |
|-------|-------------|----------------|
| Jobs, economy | 20 % (✓ >12 %) | 18 % (✗ >14 %) |
| Immigration | 11 % (✗ >12 %) | 15 % (✗ 10‑14 %) |
| Housing | 21 % (✓ >12 %) | 7 % (✗ 10‑14 %) |

No single issue satisfies the requirement of being >12 % in Los Angeles **and** 10 %–14 % in the Central Valley.

**Conclusion**

From the 2018 PPIC survey, only “Jobs & the economy” and “Immigration” exceed 9 % overall. However, **no issue meets the dual regional criteria** (over 12 % in Los Angeles and between 10 %–14 % in the Central Valley).
